To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) jet heating can be successfully implemented with high-resolution simulations using low-diffusion hydro solvers and (ii) the simulations suffer from a lack of convergence that is a consequence of thermal instabilities that develop at the grid scale.

(1) jets provide a significant amount of heating, but only near the jet axis; (2) turbulence provides a small amount of additional heating, but only at the cluster centre; and (3) weak shocks provide the dominant source of heating, and are distributed over a larger volume, but their heating rate depends on the choice of hydro solver.

(1) the heating rate in the jet is anisotropic, with a maximum near the jet axis; (2) the heating rate is mostly provided by weak shocks, with a small contribution by turbulence; (3) the heating rate depends on the choice of the numerical scheme, and (4) the simulations suffer from numerical convergence problems.
